# HyperFrames v0.9.50

Released on 2026-11-15.

Renders now read only the media and files that belong to them, including every playlist a playlist names. Lambda renders reach only public addresses by default, like the other cloud render paths, and lint rules check large files faster.

## Fixes

- **AWS Lambda:** Lambda renders reach only public addresses unless the function opts out ([e8a59bf17](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/e8a59bf1774f9880109bb7a426c55825725feb74), [#7780](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/7780)).
- **Engine:** Media playlists are checked through every list they name ([f4b6aad33](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/f4b6aad33251715e803e3bb84c24a0b446a5e956), [#7778](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/7778)).
- **Engine:** Refuse media playlists that name files outside their folder ([06cf96464](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/06cf9646463596167a5b7e41f33fa1acdc5ced0f), [#7768](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/7768)).
- Render file servers refuse env and Git files; shown-box sampling stays within the render ([603395c89](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/603395c89a680403f370be816331f1507dc9bd5c), [#7765](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/7765)).
- **Producer:** Render-service media probes stay on public HTTPS ([0e767d620](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/0e767d620f630c4993e9b12364ae6d1e11f24421), [#7764](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/7764)).

## Performance

- **Lint:** Rules scan script, style and comment blocks in linear time ([12832e3a9](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/12832e3a98138b45b94a376f9f324cb44667c5ba), [#7770](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/7770)).

## Full changelog

### Highlights

- **Large-session reliability:** reduce memory pressure during transcript indexing, trimming, and compaction; stream only selected hydration payloads and honor configurable summary limits. (#194099, #194066, #194536, #196207) Thanks @vincentkoc, @aniruddhaadak80, @RomneyDa, @garrytan.
- **Restart and delivery safety:** preserve queued-message permission ceilings and accepted ingress during restarts, drain final chat writes before handoff, and retain delivery ownership through the final RPC. (#196540, #196923, #196493, #197427) Thanks @joshavant, @vincentkoc.
- **Recovery and setup:** improve cold-start initialization, interrupted workspace recovery, installer permissions, and actionable iMessage Automation status. (#192552, #196423, #186782, #186117) Thanks @javiermv, @anmol0b, @RomneyDa, @vincentkoc.

### Changes

- **Models and tools:** restore context-sized default output budgets, expose effective deferred MCP tools with bounded input hints, and deduplicate wrapped structured MCP results. (#193899, #196766, #196252, #196266, #196243) Thanks @RomneyDa, @jalehman, @GrahamMcBain, @VACInc, @vincentkoc.
- **Compaction:** support a configurable summary-character limit while retaining foreground request-budget constraints and redacting credentials in quoted summary content. (#196207, #197349) Thanks @aniruddhaadak80, @RomneyDa, @garrytan, @obviyus.
- **Browser and workspaces:** route Lightpanda navigation through its supported connection path and wait for sandbox files to become ready. (#196400, #197248) Thanks @RomneyDa, @mmaps.

## Major performance improvements, automatic cleanup & focused subagent views ✨

Orca 1.4.259 improves performance across crowded sidebars, long chats and terminal restoration, and keeps Git reads moving while new workspaces are created. New cleanup controls help you manage the workspaces left behind.

- ⚡ **Smoother busy workspaces:** Crowded sidebars and long chat tool runs render only the visible rows, reducing rendering work and chat memory use. Terminal history restores without blocking the window on disk reads.
- 🧹 **Clear finished work on your terms:** Settings → Workspace Cleanup lets you review matching workspaces, enable automatic cleanup and inspect its activity. Give individual projects their own rules.
- 💬 **Follow one subagent at a time:** Open its task, live steps and final answer in a dedicated view, then return to the main conversation where you left off.
- 🤖 **Use Kimi Code in Chat:** Start a conversation with Kimi’s model picker, permission controls, questions and `/compact` support.
- 🎙️ **Watch dictation take shape:** Nemotron 3.5 now streams live text; Parakeet Unified EN adds an English-only streaming option. Optional AI cleanup handles punctuation and spoken corrections before insertion.
- 📱 **Find the phone tab that needs you:** The tab bar shows the open tab, a count and an add button. Tap the count for a grouped view of all tabs, including those waiting for your answer.

**Previous release: [1.4.258](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/tag/v1.4.258)** — Smoother workspaces, restored phone scrolling and Copilot Chat.

## Highlights

- **Keep working while agents use tools:** Agent-created terminal splits keep your keyboard where it was. Browser popups and new-tab links opened by agents stay in the background. A server agent’s new browser tab can open on your paired desktop; without a paired desktop, it stays on the server.
- **Organize without stopping work:** Hide a project from the sidebar while its agents, terminals and automations

## v0.5.70 - 2026-11-14

- **Security patch: fast-xml-parser 5.12.1 and fast-xml-builder 1.3.2.** Fixes a quadratic-time attribute scan in the XML validator ([GHSA-7cfw-w2rf-f3jc](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-7cfw-w2rf-f3jc)) and an uncontrolled recursion crash in the XML builder ([GHSA-g62r-xqpr-7fwx](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g62r-xqpr-7fwx)). arXiv, PubMed, and Europe PMC results parse the same as before.

body:
Security release: ten reports from eight researchers, six distinct problems, all
fixed. No new commands.

**After updating, three things behave differently:**

- **Chromium runs sandboxed where the system allows it.** On systems that
  cannot start the sandbox (Ubuntu 23.10 and later, GitHub's Ubuntu runners,
  most Docker images, root)
  pages still render, a warning says why, and the JSON result carries
  `sandbox: false`. The sandbox is best effort unless you set
  `CLAUDE_SEO_CHROMIUM_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1`, which fails instead.
- **Google sign-in is read-only by default.** A new sign-in asks for read-only
  Search Console and Analytics access. To use `indexing_notify.py`, sign in with
  `google_auth.py --auth --indexing`. Existing sign-ins keep working.
- **Screenshots and rendering no longer use a proxy on a local or private
  address**, and SOCKS or `https://` proxy URLs are refused for browser
  commands. An `http://` proxy on a public address is supported (tested against
  a simulated proxy only). If direct access is allowed, unset the proxy
  variables or use `NO_PROXY` for the audited host. An opt-in for a named local
  proxy is planned for the next release.

Also: `google_auth.py --tier` no longer lists the Indexing API for a read-only
sign-in, and `verify_release.py` now prints manifest values in quotes and fails
on an empty manifest.

### Security

- **The headless browser can no longer be redirected to local addresses**
  (GHSA-8wrm-4mmq-6fx3 by @namaserajesh, GHSA-9pc7-p6cr-942h by @Nordalux, who
  also wrote the initial fix). The earlier guard checked only the first URL of
  a request, so an audited site could redirect Chromium to loopback, private
  network or cloud metadata addresses and have the response returned in the
  audit. Every browser connection now goes through a local guard that checks
  each destination, including every redirect, and connects only to the
  addresses it checked. The guard accepts only the browser it started. Unlighthouse

Univer 1.5.0 adds dedicated chart sheets, stacked line charts, and error bars. Pro's free tier now covers more editing and local output workflows. This release also reduces memory use during formula calculation, adds controls for Sheets interactions and Board layout, and improves Office file compatibility.

## New features

### Chart sheets, stacked line charts, and error bars

Give a chart its own tab while keeping its source cells in regular worksheets in the same workbook. Move charts between sheets with undo and redo. With the Sheets Chart Facade loaded, use `workbook.insertChartSheet(info, { name, index })` to set the tab name and zero-based position, and `getPrimaryChart()` to access the main chart. A chart sheet can also continuously fit its main chart to the viewport using `zoomToFit`. Older snapshots without this setting use fixed zoom. [Chart sheets guide](https://docs.univer.ai/guides/sheets/features/charts#chart-sheets)

Create stacked and 100% stacked line charts. The chart editor and the builder and live chart APIs also support per-series error bars for basic 2D column, bar, line, and scatter charts. Use `setErrorBars()` and `clearErrorBars()` to control direction, end caps, styling, and error amounts. Supported amounts include fixed values, percentages, standard deviation, standard error, and positive or negative values from custom fields in the chart's data source. Scatter charts support separate X and Y error bars. [Error bars guide](https://docs.univer.ai/guides/sheets/features/charts#error-bars)

### Editable Board diagrams and a dedicated LaTeX package

Use `planLayout()` to arrange a diagram or adjust connector routes, endpoints, labels, and text fitting. Inspect the returned diagnostics before applying a ready plan with `applyLayoutPlan()`. Applying a plan is undoable, and the resulting shapes and connectors remain editable. Imported tree branches can be collapsed or expanded with `setTreeBranchCollapsed()`. Rendered analysis report

Changes since 1.25.2:

- Keep strikethroughs on pages that strike several lines of similar width, as tracked-changes documents do: the repeated-ruling filter only kept such a rule when it underlined the row it fits, so every one of these strikes was dropped as a table ruling. A rule that snugly strikes through one row is now kept, and the underlined row and the struck row are judged apart so neighbouring rows never combine into one owner (#663).
- Keep strikethroughs on text inside a detected table: clearing the decorations of table text exists for underlines, which a cell's bottom border imitates, and no border runs through a cell's glyphs (#663).
- Emit the strikethroughs recovered above as `<s>` without changing anything else on the page: run merging and heuristic table detection read them as before, and a word hyphenated across a line break inside a struck run rejoins across the reopened `<s>` tag (#663).
- Read a TrueType subset with no `cmap`, no glyph names and no ToUnicode that comes from a core Windows font through the Windows variant of the standard glyph order, which the font's own advances choose: `“N/A”` no longer reads as `—N/A“`, `company’s` as `company‘s` or en dashes as `œ`. A glyph past the standard order that paints nothing but advances reads as a space, so Word's justified Arial lines no longer read U+FFFD between every word (#618).

API: `TextItem::layout_strikeout` (Rust), the strikeout layout heuristics read. It equals `is_strikeout` except on the strikethroughs recovered above. Rust literals of `TextItem` must include the new field. The Node, Python and WebAssembly bindings and the `pdf2md --items-json` fields are unchanged.

Agent Skills 0.6.16 lets specs evolve past V1, teaches the docs skill to spot drift, stops the frontend skill from installing toolchains just to verify, and fixes two quality-gate examples that could never fail.

## Skills

- **Spec evolution** (#383, @ayobamiseun). Specs now carry a version and an Out of Scope (Deferred) list, and a change to a shipped feature gets its own small delta spec (`SPEC-<change>.md`) instead of a rewrite. `/spec` writes one when `SPEC.md` already exists, and `/build auto` picks the delta that isn't `Status: implemented` and refuses to run a plan generated from a different spec.
- **Documentation drift** (#514, @vyasdx). When a doc may be stale, documentation-and-adrs compares the last commit to the code with the last commit to the doc, and says "can't tell" instead of "current" when the history is unordered. Change logs are appended to, never rewritten.
- **Verify with what the project has** (#732, @TwelveNights). frontend-ui-engineering no longer installs a test runner or type checker just to check its work, and follows the WAI-ARIA APG patterns for menus, dialogs, tabs, listboxes and comboboxes. Measured +0.10 across 11 models, with package installs down from 24% to 4% of runs.
- **Review findings checked against the code** (#736, @CybotTM). code-review-and-quality checks each finding against the callers, guards and tests that reach the change, labels defects already in the base separately, and treats zero findings as a valid result.
- **Gates that can fail** (#786, @rudycelekli). `depcruise --validate src` printed usage and exited 0; the constraints skill now runs `depcruise src`.
- **Session secret** (#787, @rudycelekli). The hardening example fails at startup when `SESSION_SECRET` is missing instead of returning 500 on every request.
- **OWASP Top 10:2025** (#785, @usaid7015). The checklist and security skill use the 2025 numbering, cited with the year.
- **Skills fire on pasted code** (#762, #763, #757, @ayobamiseun, part of #620).

- **Cheaper** than vector RAG: for both index and query.
- **Faster**: trees are created from layout stats.
- **Unified** SDK: vectorless RAG. **Local** or **cloud**, for index and chat.
- Runs on your **Claude subscription**.

Index, to chat, to agent integration, one client.
Local mode needs no server, no vector DB, no PageIndex API key.

```python
client = PageIndexClient()
client.submit_document("report.pdf")
client.chat("What does the report conclude?")
```

## Highlights

- **Flash engine**: the local default (`mode="standard"` keeps the classic LLM pipeline). Embedded bookmarks are consumed when trustworthy, and tree optimization is on by default — `optimize="merge"` for the deterministic LLM-free pass, `"full"` (default) adds LLM expand, which runs a wave of nodes concurrently instead of one round-trip at a time.
- **One complete surface, local and cloud**: `PageIndexLocalClient(storage_path=...)` is the same client as cloud — submit, tree, page content, chat, and agent tools all present in both modes, so code moves between them unchanged.
- **Cloud documents, your own model**: `api_key` decides where your documents live; a configured chat model decides who answers — and the two combine. `PageIndexClient(api_key="pi-...", chat_model="openai/gpt-5.2")` runs the same in-process document-QA engine over the live cloud tool set. Page content flows through your process to your provider on your credentials; `doc_id` targets at the prompt level; `enable_citations` stays with the managed chat.
- **Agent integration**: the cloud MCP tool contract, in-process — `client.agent_tools()` (plain functions), `as_openai_tools()`, `as_anthropic_tools()`, `as_claude_mcp()`, plus one-call `openai_agent_config()` / `anthropic_runner_config()` / `claude_agent_config()` bundles and `agent_instructions()` for the system prompt. Cloud clients get the live server tool set over the MCP bridge (read-only endpoint by default); local clients get the in-process subset with the same schemas


## @astryxdesign/core

### Experimental APIs

- Adds the English strings of the Lab media player (`@astryx.mediaPlayer.*`): control names, spoken times, chapter and marker context, and previous and next track. They are Lab strings shipped in Core's locale file, as Lab ListInput's strings are; they add no public API to `@astryxdesign/core`. ([#11438](/meta/astryx/pull/11438))

### New Features

- NumberInput takes `entryErrorBehavior`, so a form can pass one value to all of its date, time, and number fields. A typed number is complete only at Enter or blur, so both values keep NumberInput's current timing: its rejection, `aria-invalid`, announcement, and `onEntryErrorChange` report appear at Enter or blur, never while a person types. Setting the prop, or FormLayout's `defaultEntryErrorBehavior`, changes nothing a person sees in a NumberInput. Pagination's page box passes `'complete'`, so a FormLayout around it never changes it. ([#11492](/meta/astryx/pull/11492))

- DateInput, DateTimeInput, and TimeInput take `entryErrorBehavior`, and FormLayout takes `defaultEntryErrorBehavior`. The prop sets when a field shows its own entry error, such as a date the calendar does not have or a time outside `min` and `max`. It does not set when validation runs, and it is not React Aria's `validationBehavior`. `'complete'`, the default, keeps each field's current timing. `'blur-or-enter'` holds the message, `aria-invalid`, the invalid styling, the announcement, and the `onEntryErrorChange` report until the person presses Enter or leaves the field; an edit that makes the entry valid or empty still clears the error at once. - **Start from a world.** `impeccable world <id>` writes that world's design system as your DESIGN.md, beside PRODUCT.md, and never overwrites one you have. Later direction rounds name the world you chose instead of dealing new ones. Needs a signed-in account.

- **Live on a first page.** In an empty folder, Live says there is no page yet and offers to craft one, instead of leaving files behind. A plain HTML page gets its one-line config written for it. The first pick works on a bare element, and a first session tells you what to click.

- **Live edits stay on their line.** Live can wrap an element that shares its line with other markup, and accepting a variant never removes the rest of that line.

- **Walkthroughs from any recording.** `impeccable walkthrough` turns a screen recording into an MP4, a poster and chapters, ready for a Needs you walkthrough card.

- **Agents that use Loop.** `impeccable loop connect` now teaches your coding agents to ask through Needs you, and tells them that Loop wakes them when you answer.

- **Foundations from your files.** `impeccable foundations` checks 16 of its 18 launch items from local files. It leaves an item unchecked when it couldn't see enough to be sure, for example a stylesheet a build hasn't produced yet.

body:
FastMCP 4.2 serves agent skills from the server. A skill used to live in a folder on each machine, so every agent kept its own copy and an update meant asking everyone to reinstall. Now the server holds one copy next to the tools the skill describes, and a deploy updates every agent that reads it.

```python
from fastmcp import FastMCP, Skill
from fastmcp.skills.provider import SkillCatalogProvider

deploy = Skill.from_directory("skills/deploy")

mcp = FastMCP("Team Skills")
mcp.add_provider(SkillCatalogProvider([deploy]))
```

Any client can read a skill's files as ordinary resources. Clients that speak the experimental [Skills extension](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/seps/2640-skills-extension) also get `skills/list`, with a hashed manifest for each skill. Few hosts support it yet, so FastMCP's client fills in: `Client.read_skill()` checks every file's size and digest, and `to_directory()` installs a skill into an agent's local skills folder. Skills work with the rest of FastMCP: they're namespaced under mounts, pass through proxies, list across a `ClientGroup`, and respect `AuthMiddleware`. The [skills docs](https://gofastmcp.com/docs/servers/skills) cover the details.

Dependencies can now be declared in the annotation, as in `Annotated[dict, Depends(get_config)]`, so the parameter keeps its real type, and a dependency can own the tool argument it reads through `CallArgument`. The rest of the release is fixes across OpenAPI, proxies, auth, telemetry and tasks. Thirteen community PRs merged during the cycle were reverted before release and are not listed here.

### Before upgrading

- Python 3.11 or newer is required.
- The 4.1 skills API is deprecated and will be removed in 4.3. The old providers in `fastmcp.server.providers.skills` and helpers in `fastmcp.utilities.skills` still work and warn with their replacement. The [skills docs](https://gofastmcp.com/docs/servers/skills) include a migration table.
- `Skill` is now the class you author with. The wire mode

## Behavior changes
- Requests to the Fetch "bad ports" (ssh, smtp, pop3, imap, …) are now refused for every request, not only WebSocket.
- `window.postMessage` now honors `targetOrigin`.
- A cross-site response can no longer set a `SameSite` cookie other than `None`.
- Proxy and server credentials are tracked separately, so proxy credentials are no longer sent to the server after a redirect.
- An `about:blank` (or src-less) iframe now gets its `contentWindow` and `contentDocument` even without `--load-resources iframe`. Its HTTP and WebSocket requests are blocked while iframe loading is off.
- An HTTP status from 600 to 999 (e.g. LinkedIn's `999`) is now reported as-is instead of `0`.
- Trusted `mousedown`, `mouseup`, `click` and `dblclick` now stop at the first disabled form control, as in Chrome.
- Element clicks and hovers from tools now hit the element's center instead of `(0, 0)`.
- `document.readyState` is now `interactive` when deferred scripts run.
- `Network.setUserAgentOverride` now logs a warning when a restricted user agent is ignored.
- The HTTP server parses requests more strictly and its routes are guarded against DNS rebinding.

## CDP
- Several page targets in one browser context. Console, exception and network events are routed to the right target, and a frame id from another target is rejected
- Accessibility: `ignoredReasons` now match Chrome (`ariaHiddenElement`, `ariaHiddenSubtree`, `inertElement`, `notRendered`, `notVisible`)
- Lone surrogate escapes in JSON (`"\udc00"`) are accepted instead of closing the connection
- `LP.waitUntil` and a `settled` lifecycle event
- `beacon` added to `LP.configureLoading`
- A closed browser context no longer leaves its viewport override for the next one
- `LP` commands described in `/json/protocol`

## Serve / CLI
- `--wait-until settled` (experimental): waits for load, then for the work that can still change the page. Interval timers, long timers and intersection observers don't hold

Run stateful agents on Kubernetes with numbers you can check. This edition adds Agent Substrate 101, a manual built from 24 recorded experiments, and moves every course lesson to a short, readable URL.

[Start learning](https://aiengineeringfromscratch.com) · [Agent Substrate 101](https://aiengineeringfromscratch.com/manual-agent-substrate-101.html) · [All manuals](https://aiengineeringfromscratch.com/manuals.html)

## Agent Substrate 101

A manual for Agent Substrate v1.0.0, with kagent 1.0, agentgateway v1.7.0 and Agent Executor. It goes from the first actor to a cluster that you can size, connect, upgrade, and debug.

| | |
|---|---|
| Sections | 40 in 9 parts, and 10 reference sections |
| Figures | 75, most of them showing each run, not only a median |
| Experiments | 24, recorded on kind clusters, with scripts and raw output in the repository |
| Summaries | 38, rebuilt and checked offline by `capture/run.py --check` |
| Demos | an idle suspender, a stateful agent, a tool sandbox, and a failure drill |

Some of what the runs found:

- An idle actor is never suspended. You build the idle policy yourself.
- 300 resumes at one time all succeeded on one node, at about 37 per second. More API server or router replicas did not raise the rate; the parallel gVisor restores on the node set it.
- `kubectl drain` crashes a running actor and leaves a suspended one unharmed. Suspend with `--mode sync`, then drain.
- With the bucket away, a synchronous suspend crashed a healthy actor. The default suspend lost nothing.
- An actor without a `SIGTERM` handler crashed at every upgrade roll, 4 of 4.
- A kagent turn has no bound by default. `maxTokens` or `timeout` on the ModelConfig sets one.

Section 1.1 sets each headline claim of the project site beside our result. Section 8.5 lists the runs coming in the next edition, with GKE first. The PDF is attached to this release as `aiefs-manual-agent-substrate-101.pdf`.

## Lessons

- Course lessons are served at `/learn/<phase>/<les

### Highlights

- **Background Subagents by Default**: Subagents now return immediately, continue in the background, and report back whenever they become idle. You can keep working in the parent session while multiple subagents run concurrently. ([#63382](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63382))
- **Quieter Transcripts by Default**: The TUI now summarizes each run of tool calls and thoughts into one collapsible activity row, so the answer is easier to follow. To see every step again, set **Verbosity** to `medium` or `high` in settings, or set `session.verbosity` in your TUI config; an existing setting is kept. ([#63207](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63207))
- **Jump to an Earlier Prompt**: In the desktop app, open **Jump to message** from the command palette or press `Cmd+Alt+G` (`Ctrl+Alt+G` on Windows and Linux) to search prompts across the current session and jump directly to one. ([#63585](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63585))

### Core

#### Improvements

- Subagents now always run in the background, return their session ID immediately, and report results to their parent whenever they become idle. ([#63382](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63382))
- Added experimental support for MCP events, behind the `mcp_events` flag. ([#63254](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63254), [#63261](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63261), [#63269](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63269))
- Shell commands now survive server handoffs and keep their output when interrupted.
- Added experimental support for moving a shell command to the background when its timeout expires, behind the `shell_timeout_background` flag. With the flag on, an explicit timeout on a background command stops it. ([#63024](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63024), [#63703](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63703))
- Local Windows shell commands now run through the process daemon.
- Added support for freeform tool inpu

body:
- **What a signed-in CLI saves.** If you sign in with `impeccable login`, a full `detect` of a git repo saves its design health counts and the foundations it found, never your code or file names. Your DESIGN.md and each critique report your agent saves upload in full, and the first upload of each tells you so and names its off command. Setup status reports once a day which coding agents have Impeccable. Each one has its own off switch (`impeccable health off`, `impeccable health design off`, `impeccable critiques off`, `impeccable setup off`), and `forget` deletes what was saved. Nothing is saved on CI.

- **Codex's design hook sees shell writes.** Codex writes most files through the shell, so the end-of-turn pass used to scan nothing in about half of sessions. It now checks every UI file changed since the session began.

- **A fair shot for every direction.** Before dealing directions for a new look, the skill asks only about the product and proposes no look of its own. A product your brief names, like Linear or Stripe, now sets the quality bar instead of fixing the style, so the dealt directions still get a fair look.

- **Audit keeps its report.** `audit` saves its findings next to critique's, and one `reports` setting turns saving on or off for both.

- **Smaller fixes.** A boot note points to `/impeccable doctor` when the design hook isn't installed. Live mode keeps page fonts in captures and keeps an accepted variant styled on static pages. The engine honors `NO_PROXY`. Subagents can reach your MCP tools. `audit` checks right-to-left layouts. Codex's plugin hooks run on Windows, thanks to @MaxFabian25 for the report and @zhangkom for the fix.
name: Skill 4.9.0

## AI Gateway capabilities are now available to every organization

- **More AI Gateway features are available to every organization.** Auth & Security, config import and export, AI Gateway API keys for other tools, custom OpenAI-compatible providers, and Smart Routers are now available to every organization, including self-hosted deployments; their completed-rollout switches are gone. TrueFoundry is also available directly in the provider picker. Organizations that had not enabled Auth & Security now have 30-day session limits and admins confirm their identity after 15 minutes for sensitive changes. Claude prompt caching also lowers the cost of long sessions through AI Gateway.
- **Admins have clearer controls for roles and computers.** Admins can assign built-in or custom roles to people or teams, and members can disconnect signed-in computers and set what other devices may do on each one. New sandbox organizations make joiners super admins by default. The My Sessions pages have been removed from Den, and a member's Workbot cloud computers are deleted when they leave an organization.
- **Workbot and remote tasks recover more cleanly.** Workbot can hand over apps as cards, recovered tasks no longer show as failed, and remote tasks can bring questions and computer-use approvals back to the chat that started them. _Automated prerelease from `develop` — **Server** v3.6.0._


### Added
- **ai, client-python, client-typescript**: native tool calling. A `Question` with a non-empty `messages` list, and optional `tools`, is sent to the model as real provider turns, and `Answer.fromResult` returns the model's message, its tool calls and a stop reason. The Anthropic, OpenAI and OpenAI-Compatible API nodes support it, and any other LLM node answers with `tools_unsupported` before calling its model. Tool names keep their dots: the engine maps them to names each provider accepts and maps calls back. The prompt node keeps a turn's conversation and tools, and the guardrails node checks a turn's last user message and the arguments of its tool calls. A `Question` without `messages` works as before (#2838)
- **client-python**: `rocketride --version` prints the installed package version
- **mcp**: every HTTP MCP tool now declares explicit `readOnlyHint`, `destructiveHint` and `openWorldHint` annotations, the server sends `instructions`, the four core workflow tools ask Claude Code to load them upfront (`anthropic/alwaysLoad`), and the engine serves OpenAI's plugin domain-verification token at `/.well-known/openai-apps-challenge` from `MCP_OPENAI_APPS_CHALLENGE_TOKEN` (404 while unset) (#2997)
- **docs**: a Cloud Databases page under Deploy & Operate says what an app owner gets from the `rocketride_sql`, `rocketride_vector` and `rocketride_graph` databases: one per organization shared by its members, plus team and personal ones, and none per app; up to 6 transactions at once per database and no storage, table or query-rate quotas; uninstalling an app leaves its tables, while a member leaving or a team or organization being deleted retains a database for 30 days before a final dump and deletion; backups configured for whole-cluster point-in-time recovery over 30 days; and no export. `ROCKETRIDE_APPS.md` gives app agents the short version (rocketride-saas#788)
- **appdev, vscode**: an app create

### Fixed

- **Installed agents show valid JSON in their output examples (#203, from @rsloveless).** The instruction-critic, readability-recommender and corpus-critic templates kept `str.format()` brace escapes, but none of the three goes through `.format()`, so a clean install wrote `{{` and `}}` into their JSON schema examples, on both the Claude and Codex targets. An agent that copied its example emitted invalid JSON. The escapes are gone from those three templates, and a new test installs every agent for both targets and parses each fenced `json` example.
- **`run verify` leaves the Sources section out of citation density (#202, from @SID-6921).** The `citation-density` gate counted every `[N]` and `[[...]]` in the whole report, including the numbered entries of `## Sources` / `## References`, so a long source list could carry a thinly cited body over the floor. The gate now counts citations and words in the body only, matching cite-check and the instruction critic. The length, heading and scaffold-leak checks still read the full report.
- **Sync picks the same winner for duplicate note ids on every filesystem (#201, from @jackiectl2).** Sync scanned notes in `rglob` order, so when two files declared the same `id:` the one kept depended on directory traversal order; an import of `a/note.md` and `b/note.md` could keep `b`. Sync now scans in lexical path order.

## Critical fixes

- **Codex keeps recording after claude-mem updates** (#6058, thanks @wiesenthal). Codex approves a hook that ships inside a plugin against a fingerprint of the plugin's whole folder. Every claude-mem update rewrites that folder, so after every update Codex switched all seven claude-mem hooks off ("plugin contents changed; hook approval required") and Codex sessions stopped being saved, with no message. The installer now registers claude-mem's Codex hooks in your own `~/.codex/hooks.json`, and each hook runs the on-PATH `claude-mem` launcher, which finds the newest install by itself. Codex trusts a hook in `hooks.json` by its own definition and position, so one approval now lasts across updates. Other tools' hooks in that file are kept in place, a second install changes nothing, a `hooks.json` that can't be parsed is refused and left untouched, and uninstall removes only claude-mem's entries. Turning the claude-mem plugin off in Codex still stops capture. `npx claude-mem doctor` has a new `Codex hooks` row that warns when the plugin is on but its hooks are missing from `hooks.json`.

  **Codex users: do this once after updating.**
  1. Run `npx claude-mem install` and select Codex. `npx claude-mem update` and auto-update don't move the hooks, because older installers saved no agent selection. The installer prints `Registered 7 claude-mem hooks in <codex home>/hooks.json`.
  2. Open interactive Codex, run `/hooks`, and approve the seven claude-mem hooks. `codex exec` can't ask for approval, so do this in interactive Codex first.

  After that, updates don't need a new approval. Codex asks again only when a claude-mem hook's definition changes, when claude-mem adds a hook, or when another tool's hook listed before claude-mem's is removed.

## Contributors

@Vidit-Ostwal, @gabemilani, @github-actions[bot], @lorenzejay

## Commit-pinned installation

Copy the complete command for your operating system into PowerShell (Windows) or Terminal (macOS/Ubuntu). Use the same command to install or update.

### Windows 11 x64 or ARM64

```powershell
$commit="63bbb50111713b02f3bc0ebbd5f354f4eb038f99"; $env:SKILL_RECORDER_COMMIT=$commit; irm "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/skill-recorder/$commit/install.ps1" | iex
```

**Windows now finishes installation without opening the app.** Follow the prominent `@`-bordered completion notice: finish recording, choose **Quit** in every running Skill Recorder copy, wait for them to close, then open **Skill Recorder (Source)** from the desktop or Start menu. If shortcut creation fails, use the manual launch command printed by the installer. Reopen the app, not the installer.

### macOS or Ubuntu

Quit older running copies before updating, then run:

```sh
commit="63bbb50111713b02f3bc0ebbd5f354f4eb038f99"; curl -fsSL "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/skill-recorder/$commit/install.sh" | SKILL_RECORDER_COMMIT="$commit" bash
```

body:
## Critical fixes

- **Gemini CLI on Windows records again** (#6079, thanks @tanishqbaweja). On Windows, Gemini CLI runs hook commands through PowerShell. The hook commands claude-mem wrote started with a quoted path, which PowerShell rejects as a parser error. Every claude-mem Gemini hook (SessionStart, BeforeAgent, AfterTool, AfterAgent, SessionEnd) failed on every event since 15.18.0, so Gemini sessions on Windows saved nothing and got no saved context. Hook commands on Windows now start with PowerShell's `&` call operator, as the Cursor and Windsurf hooks already do. macOS and Linux are unchanged.

  **Windows Gemini CLI users: run `npx claude-mem gemini install` once after updating.** `npx claude-mem update` and auto-update do not rewrite Gemini's hooks, so the broken commands stay until you reinstall them. The reinstall replaces the old commands, and `npx claude-mem gemini uninstall` removes both forms.

## Improvements

- **My Work shows the real state of open work** (#6038). Jev now reads each open work-state item once per version on the 10-minute My Work check and labels it: the state its notes describe, plus which of its fields holds the next step and the result. At confidence 0.8 or higher, My Work shows a judged status in place of a quiet agent's stale `doing` or missing status (finished becomes Done, not checked; waiting on you becomes Needs you; abandoned becomes Closed). A status the agent set on purpose, such as `blocked`, is kept. Labels are stored in `work-view/work-state-labels.json`; the work-state log itself is never written. Notes are redacted before Jev reads them, calls are paced one a second, and a service refusal or outage stops the run without being retried until the next check.

## CI

- The integration lane launches Chrome once before its tests, so the first browser test no longer fails on the runner's slow first Chrome start (#6070, thanks @bulanovk, fixes #6069).

## Critical fixes

- **The worker no longer fails to start when the database is busy at startup** (#6041). If the My Work refresh record was left as "running" by a restart and the database was locked at that moment, the repair write threw and took down the worker's whole startup, so memory stayed off until the next restart. The repair failure is now logged, and the next scheduled check tries again (whether or not scheduled refresh is on).
- **`npx claude-mem update` and the daily auto-update keep your setup** (#6045). Before this, an unattended update reset a server or server-beta runtime back to the local worker, so capture moved off your server. A legacy install with no saved provider could also have its cloud sync turned off and its Anthropic env keys cleared. Updates now reuse your saved runtime, provider, model and agents. They don't reopen the browser setup or ask the setup questions again, and only ask for a Gemini or OpenRouter key if one is missing. `npx claude-mem install` is unchanged.
- **My Work summaries stop retrying unusable model answers forever** (#6039, thanks @mohitdixit02, reported by @adminwat in #6037). When the model's answer failed validation, wasn't JSON or came back empty, the same unchanged request was resent every minute with no end. One report measured 104,869 calls, and the constant load starved a local Ollama runner. Each request version now gets at most 3 tries with a growing wait, then waits until its input or settings change. The card shows the actual reason. Thanks @balabommablock-cpu for testing and finding the empty-answer case.

## Fixes

- **Lower observer cost by default** (#6031, thanks @kartik70, closes #5023). The observer's conversation budget drops from 400,000 to 100,000 characters (about 100K to about 26K tokens per turn in the issue's measurement). Installs that still hold the old shipped default move once; a value you set yourself is kept.
- **Redaction:** Heroku API keys and Atlassian API tokens are now removed befo

- **Session context:** each turn starts with the recent timeline from your memory. It is refreshed every turn under one message id, so it replaces itself instead of piling up.
- **Recall each turn:** one search before the turn, as before.
- **Recording is now on by default.** After each completed turn the provider sends the prompt, one observation per tool call, and a turn summary to cmem.ai as platform `eve`. Recorded tool calls and summaries come out of your cmem.ai observer allowance, the same allowance your other clients use. Pass `capture: false` to keep the old read-only behaviour; session context, recall, search and `remember` keep working.
  - `<private>…</private>` regions and secret-shaped text are removed on your deployment before anything is sent, with the same rules the Cowork plugin uses.
  - Replays of the same turn are dropped by cmem.ai (turn-scoped tool call ids and an idempotency key).
  - Each request is sent once. No retry, spool or queue, so an outage never creates spend later. A failure is logged with how many events were accepted.
- **Tools:** `search`, `timeline`, `get_observations` (the three-step Smart search) and `remember`.
- **eve versions:** tested on eve 0.84.0 and 1.0.0-rc.9.
- **Template:** works on a free-credit Vercel AI Gateway (Claude, falling back to `openai/gpt-5-mini` when Claude is refused on free credits), or set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` to call Claude directly and `EVE_MODEL` to pick an exact model. Scheduled runs get the owner's memory, owner email must match exactly, and a morning-digest example schedule ships turned off.

Docs: https://docs.claude-mem.ai/eve-integration

A standard install now sets up the runtime in the terminal, then opens the local web setup to choose agents and integrations, bundled skills, model,

### Settings, reorganised
- **Three groups, always in the same order:** the place you are in (This computer or a Cloud), Your account, and This app. Every page says what it applies to.

### Put a site or web app online
- **Publish to Netlify.** A bot can put a site or web app online on your own Netlify account.

## Open sessions keep capturing after an update

Since 15.16.0 the worker clears old plugin versions out of Claude Code's plugin cache five minutes after it starts and then hourly. A Claude Code session that was already open when an update arrived keeps running from the older version folder. Once the sweep deleted that folder, Claude Code refused to run every claude-mem hook for that session ("Plugin directory does not exist"), so the session silently stopped saving prompts, tool calls, observations and summaries.

The sweep now reads the `.in_use` records Claude Code keeps for each plugin version, and keeps a version while any session loaded from it is still running. Folders no running session uses are still removed on the next sweep, so the disk clean-up from 15.16.0 stays. The worker's sweep, `npx claude-mem prune` (and its `--dry-run`) and the installer all follow the same rule (#5971, thanks @rigel905, fixes #5970).

## Fixes

- **Context:** an explicitly empty project selection shows nothing instead of observations from every project (#5866, thanks @Afloat16).
- **Context:** read-cost and savings estimates count stored facts once, instead of counting extra escape characters and an invented `[]` for rows without facts (#5980, thanks @Afloat16).
- **Observer:** a streamed answer that arrives as a refusal counts as generated output, so an interrupted stream is not sent again and charged twice (#5843, thanks @Afloat16).
- **My Work:** the API agent rejects an answer the provider cut with `content_filter`, instead of saving an incomplete report (#5878, thanks @Afloat16).
- **Sync:** a pulled page of synced records waits for another writer instead of failing at once with "database is locked", so a large first pull no longer backs off for minutes (#5996).
- **My Work:** the worker reads My Work's shared history once per change instead of re-reading all of it on every sync pass (#5986).

body:
### Security

- Updated the IP-address parser to fix a regular-expression denial of service affecting address parsing in rate limiting and proxy connections.
- Failed MCP responses now have a total size limit even when they use an event stream, preventing oversized error responses from being buffered without a bound.

### Added

- In the desktop app's **This computer** mode, bots can see and use Mac and Windows apps when **Let bots use this computer** is enabled. Screen access is limited to owner-started chats and asks for approval on the first use of each app in a Space ([computer](docs/computer.md)).
- See subscription allowances, reset times and remaining credits in the account menu and Settings > Usage, with the same breakdown on the mobile account screen.
- Voice connections can reuse a supported model sign-in for speech and transcription instead of requiring another key ([voice and calls](docs/voice-and-calls.md)).
- Added another optional remote computer adapter with suspend and resume support ([computer providers](docs/self-host-sandbox-providers.md#instabox-computers)).
- Mobile now offers French, Hebrew, Hindi, Korean, Brazilian Portuguese and Turkish; Hebrew uses a right-to-left layout.
- Owners can delete an unpaid organization from the plan choice, with the existing type-the-name confirmation.
- Operators can cap an account's total hosted model-credit usage without deactivating it ([billing](docs/self-host-billing.md)).

### Changed

- Deleting a bot on web or desktop names the group chats that will also be deleted, including their messages, files and pages.
- Bots retain earlier conversation by token budget rather than stopping at eight exchanges, helping them follow decisions made earlier in a chat. Longer retained history can use more input tokens.
- Bots receive a description of their Docker computer's tools and limits before starting work, and can offer the computer card when you need to see or scan its screen.
- Admin-granted credit now includes

## @claude-flow/cli, claude-flow and ruflo 3.76.0

### New (opt-in)
- **Nearest-centroid agent router (ADR-527, #4953).** Set `CLAUDE_FLOW_ROUTER_CENTROID=1` to route tasks to agents by nearest centroid over labelled examples. On the ADR-391 test split it picked the right agent 63.7% of the time, against 25.7% for the current default. The default router is unchanged. Before it becomes the default, it still needs a cost-per-verified-solve test on fresh tasks.

### Fixes
- **Neural router assets now ship in the npm package (#4958, fixes #4954).** With `CLAUDE_FLOW_ROUTER_NEURAL=1`, an npm install now loads the bundled KRR model, the low/med/high bucket specialists and their calibrators, and the seed rows. Before this, only a repo checkout could load them.
- **darwin pin moved to `~0.14.0` (#4956, fixes #4952).** This fixes the `clean-install` and `pin-drift` CI failures. Without a surrogate config, darwin 0.14.0 behaves as 0.13.1.
- **Bridge pins agentic-flow to stable 3.5.4 (#4948).** It now lists only the tools that version exposes.
- **Witness reports an unbuilt checkout as "not built" (#4946, #4885).** Real failures are no longer hidden behind that state.
- **MetaHarness bench parity (#4949, #4930).** A 404 in the digest is no longer misclassified as degraded.
- **`task_complete` credits only the worker still holding the task (#4964).** Completing a reopened task again no longer counts the same work twice. Thanks @kevin9327.
- **The settings risk scanner flags `node`, `deno`, `bun` and `php` allow-rules (#4961, #4960).** `ruflo init --upgrade` now warns when a project pre-approves these interpreters, as it already did for `python`, `ruby` and `perl`.
- **`hooks route` shows "centroid" as the method** when the centroid router decides, instead of "keyword".

### Dependencies
- `@claude-flow/memory` 3.3.2 and `agentdb` ^3.10.0 (#4955).

The `alpha` and `v3alpha` dist-tags stay at 3.75.2 (ADR-513).

🤖 Generated with [RuFlo](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo)
name: v3.76.0 — opt-in centroid agent router, neural router assets shipped

## v0.5.68 - 2026-11-11

- **pi-subagents 0.88.0.** A child waiting for your answer no longer runs out its `timeoutMs` while it waits, and a reply cut off at the model's output limit now fails instead of passing as a success. The subagent widget and `status` show the latest progress a running child reported. Copies of the parent session written by forked subagents are now deleted after `artifactConfig.cleanupDays`, so they no longer fill the disk. Also fixes Windows machines that block PowerShell and gateways that require a prompt cache key.
- **Paper search accepts `sort: "citation"`.** `feynman_science_database_search` recommends Semantic Scholar's default citation-count sort, and some models then passed `sort: "citation"`, which failed validation. The tool now treats `citation`, `citations` and `citation_count` as that default.

## What's new in 0.1.153

### Burst mode
- **Give a bot a big job and let it split the work.** Type `/burst`, or let the bot offer it: it previews the parts, runs them side by side and gives you one result. Every plan has it, with more parts at once on bigger plans.

### Models and engines
- **Ollama, found for you.** MausBot finds Ollama running on your computer and adds it in one click, shows the models you've pulled, and lets you turn a model's thinking off or pick its level.
- **Reasoning levels for OpenAI and OpenRouter API models.**
- **Star a model** to keep it at the top of its provider.
- **Amazon Bedrock** as a way to run Claude.
- **New models without an update.** The model list now refreshes by itself.

### My Cloud
- **Choose which bots move to My Cloud.** With two or more bots you pick, or move everything.
- **Big workspaces finish moving,** including on slow connections.
- **Open one of your computers from another over Tailscale,** and see why when it can't connect.
- **Bots know which of your computers they can use,** and say so when one is away.

### Phones
- **A clear notice when an older phone app stops connecting away from Wi-Fi.** Update the app on your phone, then open it once on the same Wi-Fi as your computer. Phone & devices has a **Pair again** button if you need it, and your bots now give the same answer.
- **Self-hosted servers can pair a phone through MausBot's relay,** with no domain or open port. Start the server with `--relay`. It is new: tell us how it goes.

### Hand-offs and Inbox
- **Finished hand-offs get a line in your Inbox.**
- **Work waiting on you gets one reminder after a day and closes after three,** instead of waiting forever.
- **An approval nobody answered stays in your Inbox** until you decide.

### Apps and secrets
- **Suggested apps** to connect, and bots can search the app catalog.
- **MCP server secrets are kept in the Vault,** and your saved secrets travel with you when you send a workspace to My Cloud.

# GEOFlow v3.2.1

GEOFlow 3.2.1 增加专题生产、链接投放和提示词实时测试，扩展知识导入、平台辅助发布与 AI 可见性分析。已受管站点使用配套的 Updater 0.5.0。

## 新增与改进

- **专题内容生产**：组合文章、创建 AI 专题任务、审核发布和定期维护。专题可显示在导航、首页及文章回链中。
- **链接池与提示词**：设置链接投放活动、预览推荐和查看点击统计；用未保存的提示词草稿试跑生成、知识检索和 AI 诊断。
- **知识导入与配图**：导入 PDF、PPTX 文本，结合图片备注和标签选图。扫描件及纯图片文档需先进行 OCR。

Deterministic checks ported from web-obs, the sister crawler project. Work
that the skills asked the model to do by hand (count sitemap URLs, compare
served and rendered HTML, read a certificate, check a page's basics) is now
done by scripts with tests. Two new scripts, 63 in total.

**After updating, run `/seo setup` once** (one new dependency, PySocks).

**Drift baselines:** a page whose JSON-LD script tag is typed in upper case or
with a parameter (`application/ld+json; charset=utf-8`) was skipped before and
is read now, so it shows one schema change. Re-baseline after updating.

### Added

- **`page_checks.py`: 47 on-page checks in one script.** Title, description,
  headings, canonical, robots, hreflang, document basics, images, links, URL
  hygiene, size, Open Graph, JSON-LD validity and thin content. Each finding
  has a stable id, a severity, a message and trimmed evidence. Length
  thresholds follow `quality-gates.md` and are worded as display heuristics,
  not Google rules. `/seo page` runs it first.
- **`transport_check.py`: TLS certificate, security headers and redirects.**
  Certificate validity, days to expiry, host and www coverage and trust;
  grades for HSTS, CSP and the other security headers plus cookie flags (by
  cookie name, never the value); the http to https and www redirects. The TLS
  socket connects only to the address the safety layer validated and is
  skipped behind a proxy. `/seo technical` runs it for its security section.
- **`sitemap_discovery.py --expand`.** Follows a sitemap index one level and
  reports, per file and in total: URL counts, lastmod quality (missing,
  oldest, newest, share of identical dates), entries on another host,
  duplicates, and the 50,000 URL and 50 MiB limits. `--max-children`
  (default 50) and `--sample` (default 20) bound the run. `sample_urls` are
  exact and can be status-checked; URLs carrying a token or session
  parameter are counted and shown redacted, never sampled.
- **`js_gap` in `render_page.

The sheet presentation keeps its own sheet. (#10624)

- A swizzled component and the package's components now announce through one pair of live regions: messages from both join the same frame, and a copy no longer mounts a second pair that screen readers would read twice or skip. Community fixes: 39 pull requests from 18 contributors, 6 dependency updates, and the follow-up fixes found while reviewing them. No new commands. **After updating, run `/seo setup` once.** The dependency floors changed (urllib3 2.8.0 fixes three advisories), so the managed runtime rebuilds. **Drift baselines:** three parser fixes change stored values once. A page with a JSON-LD `@graph` shows one `schema_modified` warning, and a heading that holds an inline tag or a `
` shows one heading change. Re-baseline after updating. ### Security - **urllib3 floor raised to 2.8.0** (#323). It fixes GHSA-8988-9cw3-xx77 (HTTPS proxy TLS settings ignored), GHSA-vxq7-64xx-v4gw (unbounded chunk-size buffering) and GHSA-gh4c-6fx4-qh6g (chunked deflate loop). - **A `host:port` entry in `CLAUDE_SEO_LOCAL_TARGETS` now holds for the whole request.** The DNS pin on a non-public address answered for every port, so a redirect from the allowed dev server could reach another service on that host. It now answers only for the validated port, or another port the allowlist names. Public hosts are unchanged. The port-bound pin was first proposed by @joachimBrindeau in #318. - **Google property selection is bound to the audited domain** (#387 by @dajiaohuang, issue #337 by @tomkor). `gsc_query.py`, `gsc_inspect.py` and `ga4_report.py` take `--domain` and refuse to use another site's property. `www.` and subdomains of a domain property match their `sites` entry, lookalike hosts are refused, and an empty `--domain` is an error (raised by @agammann). With a `sites` mapping and no flag, the scripts stop and ask for `--domain` or `--property`; `gsc_inspect.py --batch` needs one of `--site-url` or `--domain`. - **IndexNow key check compares hosts, not URL substrings** (#371 by @rudycelekli). `example.com` no longer matches `notexample.com`. The key file must be on the submitted host exactly. - `commoncrawl_graph.py --release` rejects a value with a trailing newli
name: v2.5.1: 45 community fixes, urllib3 security floor

## What's new in 0.1.152

### Advanced mode is back
- **Choose Simple or Advanced again.** The switch is back in the app. If you were on Advanced before 0.1.151, you're put back on it.

### Starter: as many bots as you like
- **No more stopping at 5 bots on Starter.** Create any number; 5 stay awake at a time and 2 work at once, as the plan page says. A bot made past the five starts paused, and one tap swaps it in for the one you use least. Nothing you're using is ever paused to make room.

### ModelGo
- **ModelGo is a new AI provider.** Add a ModelGo API key in Settings and pick from the models your key offers. ModelGo sponsors MausBot, and you'll see a one-time card about it.

### Teams
- **Each person's own view.** On a team, unread marks, notifications and bot order are yours alone.
- **See who's here.** See who is online and who has a shared chat open.
- **Connection health for admins.** A Team Cloud tells its admins how each connection is really doing.

### Your computer and your Cloud
- **See what's keeping this computer from your Cloud.** The app now says what is in the way instead of only failing to connect.
- **Lent computers survive a Cloud waking up.** Your Cloud waits for them to come back, and work handed on from your own line keeps the computer you lent.
- **Phone & devices explains an ended secure link.** If an older phone app's link has ended, the desktop says why and what to do: update the phone app and pair again.

### Small things that help
- **Ollama shows as Ollama.** Its own mark, the models you've pulled, and a plain reason when it can't answer.
- **Memory lock notice.** You're told the moment a bot's memory locks, with an Allow card.
- **MCP sign-ins.** The app says which MCP server needs a sign-in, and Test no longer passes when every call is refused.
- **AI provider keys are kept in the desktop's encrypted store.**
- **Connected apps with your own key.** With your own Composio key, connected-app traffic stays off the managed service.

### Security

- Mobile discards sign-ins that finish after a server change, preventing the previous server's session credentials from reaching the new server. Offline sign-out now retries session revocation when connectivity returns; Android also suppresses bot notifications while signed out. On iOS, old notification previews can still appear until revocation reaches the server.
- Credentials passed in local MCP server launch arguments are hidden from tool output, errors and run history, including authorization flags, numeric secret values and passwords in URLs.
- Incus computers explicitly start as an unprivileged user, including custom images without a declared user. Remote command working directories stay within the bot workspace, and team-chat attachment names are sanitized before entering bot context.
- Computer helpers no longer load Python code from the bot-writable home directory or inherit the control token when starting commands, protecting saved logins and payment details.
- The desktop computer viewer can no longer read the host clipboard. Copying from the bot's computer to the host clipboard is disabled; pasting into it remains available.
- Calls ask for voice consent before recording audio for hosted transcription, including calls without a greeting.
- Bot edits to pages shared by link now follow approval rules and show the proposed changes before publishing them. **Never ask** still saves without a prompt.
- Hardened bot email authentication and send limits, encrypted existing inbox content when content encryption is enabled, and prevented untrusted attachments from replacing existing files. Deactivated owners no longer receive bot email.

```bash
OLD_VERSION=0.7.11  # replace with the Core version your project uses today
npm install @astryxdesign/core@0.7.12 @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12  # plus every other @astryxdesign/* package you use, at 0.7.12
npx @astryxdesign/cli upgrade --from "$OLD_VERSION" --apply --path .
```

## @astryxdesign/core

### New Features

- BottomSheet: at rest, a sheet's content starts below the grab bar whatever its `padding`, so the first line is no longer drawn through the bar's fade. The block-start inset is never less than the bar's height (`--spacing-6`): the band under the bar is not padding a child escapes, so a lone `Section` starts below the bar too; scrolled content still passes beneath it. A sheet at the default padding starts its content 8 px lower, one with `padding={0}` starts it below the bar, and one whose only child is a `Section` starts that Section 24 px lower and grows by the same amount. Core's own `padding={0}` sheets (the touch date and time pickers, the DropdownMenu and ContextMenu sheets, and the PowerSearch and Tokenizer sheets) no longer reserve that band themselves, so the pickers, PowerSearch and Tokenizer look the same and a menu's first row sits 8 px lower. The CLI's `table-filter` and `table-inbox` page templates drop their own band too, so it is not doubled. (#8558)

  _Also released in `@astryxdesign/cli`._

- ChatLayout keeps its composer on top of the software keyboard where the visual viewport shrinks for it, instead of leaving it underneath until the browser scrolls the whole page. In Chrome on Android the dock rides Gboard's measured slides up and down, in step with the keyboard. In Safari on iOS (in the browser and as a home-screen app) and in Firefox for Android, it moves above the keyboard once the browser reports it. FastMCP 4.2.0a4 requires Python 3.11 or newer and adds `Annotated` dependencies. `Depends(...)` and built-ins such as `CurrentContext()` can now be declared as `Annotated` metadata, so a type alias like `Config = Annotated[dict, Depends(get_config)]` works across tools, resources, and prompts. Skill discovery over plain resources no longer lists a nested supporting `SKILL.md` as its own skill, and `download_skill` URIs now encode manifest paths.

Since a3, the redirect URI helpers normalize raw strings the way browsers read them, the joserfc and Authlib floors pick up security fixes, and fixes land for OpenAPI request bodies, CIMD redirect URIs, multi-select elicitation schemas, search indexing, and docstring parsing. Skills support remains experimental; this prerelease is intended for integration testing.

# Hermes Agent v0.23.1

**Release Date:** November 9, 2026

> Patch release. This tag rolls up the ~618 PRs merged since v0.23.0 into a stable release for the GitHub release (CLI and installers), the Microsoft Store app, Docker and Hermes Cloud. Full curated notes for this window ship with v0.24.0.

**What this patch ships for plugin users:** since the plugin catalog's site deploy on November 9, the published `plugin-catalog.json` was larger than the 2 MiB cap clients accept, so every install silently fell back to the catalog it shipped with. `hermes plugins install <name>` could not find plugins added since your last update, installed the pin your release shipped instead of the current one, and missed newer `removed` entries. This release raises the cap to 16 MiB, so the live catalog is used again ([#151860](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/151860), fixes [#151856](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/151856), thanks @100yenadmin). Installs that stay on v0.23.0 or older keep falling back until they update.

<!-- HERMES_BUILDS_TABLE -->

## About this release

Measured at commit `3b421578588`, the window since v0.23.0 contains **2,578 non-merge commits** across **2,781 changed files** (+151,690 / −62,595), **618 merged PRs** and **409 closed issues**.

Also in the window, undocumented here on purpose: Esc backtrack in the TUI and classic CLI (replacing the rewind list picker), group chats that run on a gateway without Desktop and can seat bots from other computers, saved gateway connections shared by Desktop and the Webapp, signing the in-app browser in with your real browser profile and filling saved logins from its address bar, `hermes gateway attach` for local clients, `hermes clipboard image --json`, new plugin API (session-scoped environment values, plugin JSON-RPC methods and events, `llm.oneshot` auxiliary tasks, a compression-stable `conversation_id`, an `on_session_open` hook in the gateway, a `post_curator_run` hook), faster

## 这一版改了什么

女娲的目标从「造出来像不像」改成「比不装 Skill 的模型多出什么」。

**先写先验快照**：调研之前，先把模型不查资料就知道的内容写下来。调研只找三种东西：推翻它的、比它深的、它没有的。

**产物分三层**：350 行以内的 SKILL.md、案例库 `references/casebook.md`、原话库 `references/voice.md`。新增招式（遇到某类问题他具体怎么做）、常见误读、边界三格，每个 Skill 自带七条运行纪律，比如「材料里没有，不等于他没说过」「原话和推演分开说」。

**验证改成盲测**：独立 agent 用同一组任务题，带 Skill 和不带 Skill 各答一遍，评审不知道哪份是哪份；再加封存题和边界题。结果写进 FIDELITY.md，输了也照写。

**两种走法**：能力强的模型按每一步的过关条件放手做，轻量模型照 `references/` 里的手册一步步走。女娲自己的 SKILL.md 从 696 行压到约 240 行。

**升级旧 Skill**：对 v1.x 造出来的 Skill 说「升级XX」，调研底稿还在就不用重新调研。

**质检脚本重写**：`scripts/quality_check.py` 改为检查结构和证据，参数可以是 Skill 目录或 SKILL.md，v1 Skill 按旧标准查，每条问题带改法；中文路径和 Windows 终端下输出统一为 UTF-8。

## 我们自己的对照

同一个人物（张一鸣）、同三道题，独立评审联网核实后盲评，满分 60：不装 Skill 26，v1 的 Skill 32，v2 由轻量模型升级 43，v2 由强模型升级 51。样本只有一个人物三道题，仅供参考。

## 注意

- 生成的 Skill 结构变了，所以是大版本。v1 的 Skill 照常能用，不必马上升级。
- `examples/` 里的示例目前仍是 v1 格式。

## 怎么更新

在安装目录里执行 `git pull --ff-only`；用 `npx skills` 安装的重新装一次。

## 这一版改了什么

**打磨环**：页面写完后，`scripts/polish.py` 按原尺寸逐屏截图，模型看着自己的截图改一轮再交。脚本只报事实：连续几屏只有文字和框、缩略图还是占位色块、打磨记录空着。

**三方向更实**：缩略图要放真标题和真内容；介绍 App 的页面必须看得见 App 的界面。

**流程更顺**：选定方向后不再额外停顿；开工前的提问从「必问清单」改为题库，最多三问；内容规范里的禁令清单改成三句判据。

body:
- **`hpr search --semantic` scores every note with one numpy matmul instead of one Python `cosine()` call each (#59).** `cosine()` did three generator passes per candidate in pure Python; at 512-dim that's ~49µs/vector, so a one-second query capped out around 15k notes (5k at 1536-dim) — well past any real vault, but the module docstring's "fine to ~50k notes" was already off by about an order of magnitude, having been written as if the vectorized loop it never got already existed. `semantic_search` now loads the stored vectors with `np.frombuffer` and scores the whole set in a single matmul, which is unaffected by a note embedded under a stale model/dimension mid-migration — it scores 0, same as `cosine()` did on a length mismatch, instead of joining the matrix. The scholarly-metadata filters and index-note exclusion added in #119 are applied in the SQL fetch before the matmul, so a filtered semantic search still only scores the filtered candidate set. Measured sub-second up to ~50k notes; larger vaults are untested. A stored all-zero vector, or an all-zero query, scores 0 with no NaN. numpy was already an unlisted transitive dependency via Crawl4AI; it's now declared directly. `cosine()` itself is untouched and still covered by its own test.
- **Sync renames a note's row in place when its `id:` changes (#159, from @fduple).** An edited `id:` went through the upsert as an insert of the new id, which `UNIQUE(notes.path)` refused on every sync; the stale row kept the old id and collided with the file that really owned it. Sync now moves the row to the new id, keeps the rows only the database holds (claims, embeddings, assets, and the `sources` and `escalations` rows for its URL), rebuilds the rest from the markdown, and frees the old id in the same pass. Updates run before adds so a new file named after the freed id indexes in one run. A rename is refused, with an error naming the file, when the frontmatter declares no id or does not parse, or when a new file named

## 🧾 Locator code in Python

A locator from [locator.normalize()](https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-locator#locator-normalize) now converts to a string as Python code. Use it with [page.get_by_ref()](https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-page#page-get-by-ref) to turn an element that an agent picks from a [page.aria_snapshot()](https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-page#page-aria-snapshot) in the `"ai"` mode into code for your test:

```python
normalized = page.get_by_ref("e2").normalize()
print(str(normalized))
# get_by_role("button", name="Submit")
```

## New APIs

- New option [`timeout`](https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-cdpsession#cdp-session-send-option-timeout) in [cdp_session.send()](https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-cdpsession#cdp-session-send).

## Notable Fixes ⚠️

- Actions such as [locator.click()](https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-locator#locator-click), [locator.check()](https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-locator#locator-check), [locator.tap()](https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-locator#locator-tap), [locator.fill()](https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-locator#locator-fill), [locator.clear()](https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-locator#locator-clear) and [locator.select_option()](https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-locator#locator-select-option) now wait for the element to be [not inert](https://playwright.dev/python/docs/actionability#not-inert). An action on an element with the `inert` attribute, or inside such an element, now times out if the element stays inert.

- Fixed `claude mcp login` printing a SEP-2352 issuer warning each time you sign in again to a server that Claude Code registered with

## What's Changed

### Discord source connector

`cocoindex.connectors.discord` indexes the messages and threads of Discord text, announcement and forum channels, using the token of a bot you create and invite to your server (`pip install cocoindex[discord]`): `DiscordChannel(app=DiscordApp(token=...), channel_id=...)`.
* `DiscordChannel.items()` yields one `DiscordMessage` per message in the channel and one `DiscordThread` per thread, active or archived, including forum posts. Both have `read_text()` for embedding
* Each run lists the channel, and only the messages and threads that changed are reprocessed; a thread's messages are fetched only when the thread reruns. `message_fields` and `thread_fields` choose which fields are exposed, and so what counts as a change
* Misconfigurations that Discord answers with an empty or text-less success (the Message Content intent off, no Read Message History) and lost access raise an error, so the channel keeps its outputs instead of having them deleted
* Two examples: semantic search over a channel (`discord_text_embedding`), and support threads turned into an FAQ knowledge base (`discord_support_faq`)

by @jerryqu-coco in https://github.com/cocoindex-io/cocoindex/pull/2695

### Google Drive: sign in with a personal Google account (experimental)

Beside a service account, the Google Drive connector can read a Drive as a personal Google account signed in once through OAuth: `GoogleDriveSource(root_folder_ids=[...], user_account=google_drive.UserAccount())`. Sign in with `cocoindex auth sign-in google-drive <client_secret.json>` (sign out with `cocoindex auth sign-out google-drive`), or call `UserAccount().sign_in(...)` from your own program. The client file comes from a Desktop app OAuth client you create in your own Google Cloud project; the connector docs walk through it. A host with no browser prints the link and takes the pasted redirect address. The sign-in asks for read-only Drive access and is stored only on your compute
name: v1.2.0

## ✨ Highlights

- **🌙 Keep the browser in the background** ([microsoft/playwright#42973](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/42973)) — connecting through the extension activated the tab and focused the browser window, taking the screen from the app you were working in. Pass `--background` alongside `--extension` (config `background: true`, env `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_BACKGROUND=1`) to leave the connected tab inactive and its window unfocused, and to open the client's new tabs in the background. With `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_EXTENSION_TOKEN` set, the connect page opens in the background too (Chrome 158.0.8127.2 or later, with the browser already running). Requires extension 0.5.0 or later. Chrome throttles timers and animation frames in background tabs. ([microsoft/playwright#43864](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/43864))
- **🗂️ Leave tabs out of the Playwright tab group** ([microsoft/playwright#43038](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/43038)) — the extension always moved the tabs a client controls into its own tab group. Pass `--no-tab-group` alongside `--extension` (config `tabGroup: false`, env `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_NO_TAB_GROUP=1`) to keep the selected tab and the tabs the client opens in their existing groups, if any. Connection approval is unchanged, each controlled tab still belongs to one client, and the extension's status page lists the controlled tabs. Requires extension 0.5.0 or later. ([microsoft/playwright#43814](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/43814))

Publishing new AAS versions to npm is paused while the maintainer account is locked. Install or update skills directly from GitHub.

### Install and update without npm

Download **Source code (zip)** from **Assets** below. Extract it outside your agent's skill directory, then copy the skill folders you want from `skills/`, including their supporting files. To update, download the newer release and replace the selected folders after backing up local changes.

With GitHub CLI and `gh skill` available, preview and install a skill for Codex:

```sh
gh skill preview sickn33/agentic-awesome-skills skills/brainstorming/SKILL.md@v20.7.0
gh skill install sickn33/agentic-awesome-skills skills/brainstorming/SKILL.md --agent codex --scope user --pin v20.7.0
```

For a pinned skill, preview the newer tag and repeat the install command with that tag and the same destination. For a skill previously installed via npm, use `--dir <your-existing-skill-directory>` in place of the agent and scope flags. Back up local changes before approving an overwrite.

Narration adds an OpenAI Realtime provider, `image_gen.py` can produce animated GIFs on OpenAI `gpt-image-2.6`, and a round of conversion and round-trip fixes stops sources from being overwritten or silently altered.

Caveman 4.1.0 is a maintenance release: bug fixes across compress, OpenCode, Hermes, Pi, the proxy and the hooks, a recovery store that no longer fills up and stops compressing, and a few small switches people asked for. caveman-compress now refuses a file with a key or token in it, and installs from skill hubs again.

### Action needed

- **`forward_headers` under a `providers.<name>` block now stops the proxy from starting.** Before, it was silently ignored: no headers were forwarded and the only symptom was an upstream 401. Configure that upstream as a compat mount instead: `compat.<name>` with `base_url` and `forward_headers`, plus `wire_dialect: anthropic` if it speaks the Anthropic protocol (see `docs/technical/configuration.md`) (#1458).
- **caveman-compress refuses a file whose text holds a credential**, such as a private key block or a cloud, Git host or model API token. Compression sends the file to your model provider, so move the secret into an env var or secret manager first. The error names the line, never the secret. Placeholders like `sk-...` or `$OPENAI_API_KEY` still compress (#1471).

### Changed

- **Old recovery handles can now expire.** The recovery store used to keep every compressed original forever, so it filled up and compression stopped (#1370). When a write would exceed the store's cap, it now frees room: typed objects of sessions idle 14 days (archived) or 30 days (any) are expired, oldest first, until the store is at 80%. Retrieving an expired handle answers `cave_expired_recovery`, and each expiry is logged in `proxy.log`. Blob recoveries never expire (#1481).

### New

- **`caveman-proxy recovery-store status|check|repair`** for a damaged `ccr.db`. A damaged store now refuses writes instead of staying corrupt across upgrades; reads keep working. Repair copies only rows whose bytes still match their hash, and moves the damaged files aside untouched. `caveman status` and `caveman doctor` point at it (#1369, #1481).

## LDR 2.0

**LDR 2.0 is our biggest architectural change yet.** We rebuilt the web layer on FastAPI and Uvicorn, hardened security across the whole app, added new search engines, and made Stop actually stop research mid-generation. It took 1,010 commits in ten weeks, from 40 contributors, 31 of them new to the project. Thank you to everyone who built, tested and reported issues.

Several defaults and API contracts changed. **Read the upgrade notes before deploying**, especially if you run LDR behind a reverse proxy or call its HTTP API from your own clients.

### ⚠️ Before you upgrade

- **Take a verified offline backup first.** 2.0 changes your databases, and v1.10.7 can't use them afterwards. LDR's built-in backups aren't a substitute (see the next point). Never start v1.10.7 on upgraded data, because doing so can delete your remaining built-in backups. Follow the [upgrade and rollback guide](https://github.com/LearningCircuit/local-deep-research/blob/main/docs/deployment/upgrading.md), which also covers failed upgrades.
- **Pre-migration backups now live in their own folder.** Each user gets `encrypted_databases/backups/<user hash>/pre-migration/`. Copy that folder out of the data directory after each user's first sign-in. With the default retention (1 backup, 7 days), the first login backup after the upgrade removes the regular backups made before it. Raise **Max Backups** and **Backup Retention (days)** first if you want to keep them.
- **Check your settings and environment overrides.** Invalid configured values now raise an error instead of silently falling back to a default. This includes bad `LDR_*` booleans (only `true/1/yes/on/enabled` and `false/0/no/off/disabled` are accepted), `llm.request_timeout` below 1 second, and `llm.max_retries` outside 0–5. The settings page, research form and API errors name the offending key.
- **Everyone must sign in again** after upgrading.

Univer 1.4.0 adds Office attachment workflows, shape merging in Slides, richer pivot filtering, and `GETPIVOTDATA`. This release also separates product-specific comment integrations and introduces several package and API migrations.

## New features

### Office attachments across Sheets, Docs, and Slides

Preserve embedded OLE files when working with Office documents, with actions to preview, download, rename, and delete attachments. Supported Office files can also be converted into independent online documents when the application provides the required collaboration, attachment, and exchange services.

Office export keeps the original embedded file by default. Applications can request the current confirmed version of a converted online document instead:

```ts
import { ExchangeFormat } from '@univerjs-pro/exchange-client';

const file = await univerAPI.exportSheetByUnitIdAsync(
    unitId,
    ExchangeFormat.XLSX,
    undefined,
    { oleAttachmentSource: 'online' }
);
```

The server must support this export option. Cross-type Office previews require the corresponding existing product UI module; conversion and preview use the existing drawing and exchange plugins.

### Merge shapes in Slides

Combine supported selections with **Union, Combine, Fragment, Intersect, and Subtract**. The operations create new shape geometry and support undo/redo and collaboration. The first selected object determines the primary formatting and the subtraction direction.

### Multiple filters and whole-day date filtering

Pivot tables and pivot charts can combine different filter categories on the same field after enabling **Allow multiple filters per field**. The option is off by default.

Fixed date filters also support **whole-day comparison**, so timestamps from the same day can match without requiring identical time values.
